items.title: kaiHEN (native homebrew + minimal CFW)
items.desc: Homebrew environment and minimal custom firmware for Switch 2. It runs native homebrew from hbmenu and includes OunceShell, a file manager with an FTP server. The current release is 20261123, which adds shared-library (dynamic linking) support for homebrew programs.
items.notes: Still a work in progress. It requires an existing Switch 2 entrypoint and an acquisition tool to start (the documented path is ns2jb's hen.cjs); do not copy the release files to the SD card yourself. It allows full access to the system and NAND, so malicious or buggy homebrew could permanently brick your console. Shipped as libkaihen 20261123 in devkitPro's [ounce] pacman repo; the GitHub releases page still lists 20261117.1 as its newest release.

items.title: ounce-devkit (Switch 2 homebrew development)
items.desc: Switch 2 support for devkitPro, including libounce, OunceVK (Vulkan, OpenGL, and OpenGL ES), libkaihen, and a CMake toolchain. Existing Switch 1 libnx homebrew that uses OpenGL or Vulkan can be compiled for Switch 2.
items.notes: Install devkitPro pacman first, then run install.sh inside the devkit repository. See its README for building homebrew and the example programs.

items.title: Switch 2 Homebrew List
items.desc: Community-maintained list of native Switch 2 homebrew applications and plugins, organized by category with download links.
items.notes: Requires kaiHEN and a supported entrypoint. Check each project's own requirements before installing; use homebrew at your own discretion.

items.title: blacklist-tool (FunctionBlackList editor)
items.desc: Native homebrew to view and modify the Switch 2 FunctionBlackList. Once kaiHEN is running through one FS-capable entrypoint, it can be used to remove blacklist blocks affecting other entrypoints or games.
items.notes: Download the .nro from the releases page and put it in the SD card's /switch folder, then launch it from hbmenu. Reboot after changing the blacklist. Changes persist across reboots and possibly factory resets. Writing the BCAT copy may lead to a console ban, so use it at your own risk.

items.title: drako3d (low-level 3D graphics API for homebrew)
items.desc: Homebrew low-level 3D graphics API for the Switch 2's Tegra T239, modelled on deko3d: devices, queues, command buffers and explicit resource management, without a state tracker in the way. 0.5.0 is the first release.
items.notes: For homebrew developers, not something you install on the console. Early, so expect API changes. Its shaders are built with the uam2 compiler, and it sits on the ounce SDK next to libounce and OunceVK.

items.title: mac2jb (Mac payload injection)
items.desc: All-in-one ns2jb and CivSwitch tool for Apple Silicon Macs. It can type and save SmileBASIC bootstrap payloads over USB, run the ns2jb jailbreak, and manage follow-up tools.
items.notes: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14+, a USB-C data cable, and an unsigned USB driver with reduced macOS security/SIP disabled. The Switch must use Ethernet and be on firmware 23.0.1. Also works for CivSwitch and other keyboard-based payload injection workflows.

items.title: Civilization 7
items.desc: General repository covering the Civilization 7 exploit.

items.title: Civilization 7 — OunceCake-Civ7 (Game Dumping)
items.desc: Tool to dump unencrypted romFS and exeFS from Switch 2 games, updates, and DLC, modified to work with Civilization 7. Supports digital games, game cards, Switch 2 Editions, and NSO titles, and serves the files over FTP.
items.notes: Requires a working civswitch-kit RPC connection and the Switch 2's local IP address. Pick a title, then connect an FTP client to port 2121 in binary mode. Only dump your own games; the tool does not provide keys or decrypt files.

items.title: Civilization 7 — CivSwitch Kit (FS Escalation)
items.desc: FS escalation path for Civilization 7 that provides arbitrary filesystem read/write and includes an example firmware dump of 90 system programs (222 MB).
items.notes:
Requires Switch 2 firmware 23.0.1 and the Switch 1 physical cartridge version 1.0.0. As defined in its README, the kit also requires a one-time homebrew install from (but not exclusively) a modded Switch 1 and a Windows PC with Node.js 20+ and Python 3.10+, with both consoles wired to the same LAN. However, technically any of the known payload input methods listed below should work, for example Rooted Android, LDN simulation, a Mac, or a Pico.
This is an early-stage development. A roughly 30% rate of success can be expected in achieving FS escalation under specific conditions, so level your expectations.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Rooted Android
items.desc: If you have a rooted Android phone, you can do it all from the phone.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Modded Switch 1 (Two Carts)
items.desc: If you have a modded Switch 1 and two Civilization 7 carts, you can use this.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Linux + Modded Switch 1
items.desc: If you have a Linux system and a modded Switch 1, you can use this method, which is faster.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Modded Switch 1 (LDN)
items.desc: The LDN method without Linux: it only requires a modded Switch 1.

items.title: Civilization 7 — ESP32 + Modded Switch 1
items.desc: If you have an ESP32 and a modded Switch 1, this is the ESP port, which is also faster than the Pico / rooted Android method.

items.title: Civilization 7 — mac2jb (Mac payload injection)
items.desc: All-in-one ns2jb and CivSwitch tool for Apple Silicon Macs. For CivSwitch it can type the chat payload via USB keyboard transfer, install the boot trigger, connect to the loader, send JavaScript payloads, and manage CivHomebrew and Moonlight. It also works for SmileBASIC and other keyboard-based payload injection workflows.
items.notes: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14+, a USB-C data cable, and an unsigned USB driver with reduced macOS security/SIP disabled. The Switch and Mac must be on the same network, the Switch language set to English (US), firmware 23.0.1, and the Switch 1 physical Civilization VII cartridge at version 1.0.0. First-time chat payload typing takes roughly 20–25 minutes.

items.title: Civilization 7 — CivHomebrew
items.desc: Homebrew launcher for Switch and Switch 2 built on CivSwitch. Browse apps, install .civapp packages over FTP, and launch them from the console, with a built-in terminal for the original JavaScript payload workflow.
items.notes: Requires the Switch 1 edition of Civilization VII, physical cartridge version 1.0.0, and an existing CivSwitch setup.

items.title: Civilization 7 — kaiHEN (native homebrew)
items.desc: Starts kaiHEN 20261114c through Civilization VII instead of SmileBASIC, using civ7-fs and CivSwitch. Once HEN is running, hold R while opening a native game to reach hbmenu.
items.notes: Requires Switch 2 firmware 23.0.1 (only tested there), Civilization VII on cartridge with CivSwitch already set up and showing "Awaiting payload", an SD card inserted, the extracted kaiHEN 20261114c release, and a Linux or macOS computer with a recent Node.js on the same network. Run: node engine/hen.cjs <console-ip> --dir /path/to/extracted/kaihen. HEN lasts until the console restarts.

items.title: Civilization 7 — CivSwitchFS-kaiHEN (semi-untethered)
items.desc: Semi-untethered kaiHEN loader for Civilization VII using CivSwitchFS. The chain is persisted once, and later Civ 7 launches automatically acquire FS and start kaiHEN without an RPC connection.
items.notes: Tested on firmware 23.0.1 with Civilization VII 1.0.0 physical cartridge and the CivSwitch Remote JS Loader. Requires Node.js 20+ with npm, a microSD card formatted FAT32 or exFAT, a Switch 2 game, and kaiHEN 20261117.1 or the SD-shaped release from this repo. Run npm install once, then: npm run persist:chain -- <console-ip>. HEN lasts until the console restarts; after a restart, load Civ 7 again.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Moonlight for CivSwitch
items.desc: Experimental Moonlight client running inside CivSwitch, letting you stream PC games to Switch 2 through Sunshine with a game library, controller input, video, and stereo audio.
items.notes: Requires the Switch 1 edition of Civilization VII, physical cartridge version 1.0.0, and CivSwitch already set up.

items.title: Civilization 7 — Jellyfin for CivHomebrew
items.desc: Unofficial Jellyfin client running inside CivHomebrew. Browse your libraries and watch media in fullscreen with controller support, using server-side transcoding and the console's native H.264/Opus player.
items.notes: Requires an existing CivHomebrew environment. Supports HTTP only (no HTTPS), so use a trusted local network or VPN. Saved credentials are stored unencrypted in the game save if enabled.

items.title: Artemis Engine games (Seedsow, Nora, Hamidashi)
items.desc: Supports the Seedsow Lullaby, Nora, Princess and Crying Cat 2, and Hamidashi Creative launchers. Seedsow Lullaby also has a separate FS exploit and kaiHEN path below.

items.title: Seedsow Lullaby — seedsow-fs-kaihen (FS exploit + kaiHEN)
items.desc: Runs the FS exploit from a Seedsow Lullaby demo or full game save and starts kaiHEN, so holding R while opening a native game launches hbmenu.
items.notes: Tested on firmware 23.0.1. Requires Seedsow Lullaby Demo or Full Game with alula's Seedsow save, an inserted SD card, and a PC on the same network with Node.js 20+. Put the console IP in tools/console-host.txt or pass --ip, and let the kit download kaiHEN or point it at an unpacked release.

items.title: Seedsow Lullaby — seedsow-semi-untethered (standalone)
items.desc: Standalone semi-untethered Lua 5.1 port of the fsp-srv + kaiHEN chain for Seedsow Lullaby. After a one-time save upload, the whole chain runs on-console with no PC, Wi-Fi, or RPC server.
items.notes: Supports the Seedsow Lullaby demo and retail full game. Requires kaiHEN files on the SD card plus an initial upload with: node tools/upload-semi-untethered.cjs --host <console-ip> while the Seedsow HTTP server is running. Afterward, launch Seedsow, press A, wait for READY, close the game, and hold R twice on a donor game. Experimental; keep a save backup. Hold - and press Y to start the stock HTTP recovery server.

items.title: Gravity Circuit
items.desc: General repository covering the Gravity Circuit exploit.

items.title: Offline update to 23.0.1 from a modded Switch 1 (Local Version Matching)
items.desc: Updates an air-gapped, stock Switch 2 to firmware 23.0.1 using only a hacked Switch 1 on HOS 23.0.1 + Atmosphère 1.12.1 and Nintendo's built-in “Match version with local users” feature — no internet connection and no exploit on the Switch 2. Validated 22.5.0 → 23.0.1 (771.5 MB), plus an optional offline exFAT activation on 23.0.1 consoles running kaiHEN.
items.notes: Experimental, no warranty. Requires Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 4.0.1 on the Switch 1 and its cartridge in the Switch 2, the 23.0.1 firmware NCAs from your own dump (299 files, not included), a PC with Python 3.8+, and ~800 MB free on the Switch 1 SD card. Delete every saved Wi-Fi network on the Switch 2 before turning Airplane Mode off, and clear a stuck update task in Maintenance Mode if you hit 2211-0525. The patches are tied to the exact module builds of HOS 23.0.1.

items.title: SmileBasic 4
items.notes: This is the original implementation of the exploit, and a lot of things have improved since then. It is better to try other implementations, such as the Firmware Dumping one, which offers the same features through the RPC server with much better results overall.

items.title: 90DNS
items.desc: Public DNS service that blocks (hopefully) all Nintendo servers to help prevent bans. Works on Switch 1 and Switch 2.
items.notes: Blocks the eShop, system updates, telemetry, social features and online play. Not guaranteed to prevent bans, so read the repository carefully before relying on it.
